The tangent and normal meet where

$$\begin{aligned} 2x+3 &= -\dfrac{1}{2}x-2\\ \dfrac{5x}{2} &= -5\\ x &= -2\\ y &= 2(-2)+3\\ y &= -1\end{aligned}$$

If $y=ax^2+bx+c$, then $y'=2ax+b$.

When $x=-4$, $y'=0$ (minimum turning point):

$$\begin{aligned} -8a+b &= 0\\ \therefore\ b &= 8a\end{aligned}$$

When $x=-2$, $y'=2$ (gradient of the tangent):

$$\begin{aligned} -4a+b &= 2\\ -4a+8a &= 2\\ \therefore\ a &= \dfrac{1}{2}\\ \therefore\ b &= 4\end{aligned}$$

When $x=-2$, $y=-1$:

$$\begin{aligned} a(-2)^2+b(-2)+c &= -1\\ \dfrac{1}{2}\times 4+4\times -2+c &= -1\\ -6+c &= -1\\ \therefore\ c &= 5\end{aligned}$$

The perimeter is two arcs ($l=r\theta$) and two straight edges of length $x$:

$$\begin{aligned} P &= 1\theta+(1+x)\theta+2x\\ &= (2+x)\theta+2x\end{aligned}$$

The area is the difference of two sectors ($A=\dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta$):

$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}(1+x)^2\theta-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 1^2\theta\\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\theta\left[1+2x+x^2-1\right]\\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\theta\left(2x+x^2\right)\\ &= \dfrac{1}{2}\theta x(2+x) \qquad (1)\end{aligned}$$

Since $P=(2+x)\theta+2x$ and $(2+x)\theta=\dfrac{2A}{x}$

$$\therefore\ P(x)=2x+\dfrac{2A}{x}$$
